Title: Rejection Sampling is Optimal for Relative Entropy Coding

Abstract—In relative entropy coding, a sender aims to design
a stochastic code such that, on input X ∼PX, the receiver
can generate a sample Y ∼PY |X. It is a standard result that
(1) this requires at least I(X; Y ) bits, (2) the lower bound is
achievable within a logarithmic gap, and (3) this gap cannot be
reduced in general. The necessity of the gap suggests that the
mutual information is not the correct information measure to
quantify the rate of relative entropy coding.
A potential alternative emerged in the work of Flamich et
al. [1], who proved a tighter lower bound of IF(X →Y ), a
quantity we call the functional information. In this paper, we
show this lower bound is tight by constructing the ring toss code,
an encoding method for rejection sampling which uses at most
IF(X →Y ) + log e bits. This demonstrates that rejection
sampling is optimal for relative entropy coding.
Our result implies that the classical mutual information lower
bound is achievable within log(I(X; Y ) + 1) + 2.45 bits in
general and within 1.45 bits for singular channels, which are
both the tightest bounds of their kind to date. Moreover, our
one-shot result also recovers Sriramu and Wagner’s asymptotic
results on the second-order redundancy of relative entropy codes.
Index Terms—Relative entropy coding, channel simulation,
rejection sampling, ring toss code, singular channels.
I. INTRODUCTION
For a pair of random variables X, Y ∼PX,Y , the goal
of relative entropy coding (also called channel simulation) is
to find a stochastic code [2] that, given an input X ∼PX,
encodes a single sample Y ∼PY |X in finitely many bits. In
doing so, the sender and receiver simulate the channel X →Y .
Formally, a stochastic code is a triplet (Z, enc, dec) where
• Z is a random variable independent of X shared by
encoder and decoder called the common randomness;
• enc : X × Z →{0, 1}* is the encoder mapping an input
and common randomness realization to a binary string;
• dec : {0, 1}* × Z →Y is the decoder mapping the en-
coder output and common randomness to a point y ∈Y.
The formal requirement of (exact) relative entropy coding is
that for all inputs x ∈X,
dec(enc(x, Z), Z) ∼PY |X=x.

Under this requirement, it can be shown that [3], [4]
I(X; Y ) ≤H(Y | Z) ≤E[|enc(X, Z)|],
(2)
where | · | is the length of a binary string. There is a long line of
research work [3]–[6] to design stochastic codes which almost
achieve this lower bound, the crowning achievement of which
is the Poisson functional representation [4], yielding
H(Y | Z) ≤I(X; Y ) + log(I(X; Y ) + 1) + 4.
(3)
This logarithmic redundancy over the mutual information is
also achieved by other schemes, including greedy rejection
sampling [3], [6] and greedy Poisson rejection sampling [7].
However, it is not possible to remove this log term, as there
exist channels for which I(X; Y ) + log(I(X; Y ) + 1) −1
bits are necessary [4], [5]. Thus, a natural question is whether
a different information measure and encoding scheme could
yield a tight bound.
In [1], progress was made in this direction by improving
the lower bound on any relative entropy code to
IF(X →Y ) ≤H(Y | Z),
(4)
where IF(X →Y ) is the functional information (see Defini-
tions 2 and 3). Note that I(X; Y ) ≤IF(X →Y ), so (4) is at
least as tight as (2). However, the lower bound in (4) has only
been shown to be achievable (within log e bits) for additive
exchangeable noise channels with finite field input [8]. In this
paper, we construct the ring toss code, an encoding method
for standard rejection sampling. We prove for general channels
that it achieves the lower bound in (4) within an additive
constant of log e, demonstrating that rejection sampling is
optimal for relative entropy coding.
Concretely, our contributions are as follows:
• We construct the ring toss code and prove that its one-
shot rate satisfies H(Y | Z) ≤IF(X →Y ) + log e. This
upper bound matches the lower bound in (4) within
an additive constant of log e ≈1.44. The algorithm
and proof are remarkably simple, relying entirely on
a changed encoding of the index returned by standard
rejection sampling.
• For a class of channels called singular channels [9], [10]
(see Definition 4), we prove that IF(X →Y ) = I(X; Y ).
Therefore, our work identifies a large class of channels

for which we can achieve constant non-asymptotic redun-
dancy over the mutual information.
• For general channels, our result implies the tighter achiev-
ability result in terms of the mutual information
H(Y | Z) < I(X; Y ) + log(I(X; Y ) + 1) + 2.45. (5)
• Finally, our one-shot result recovers the asymptotic char-
acterization of relative entropy coding in [1], [10], and is
achieved by a simpler scheme with optimal redundancy.

A. Rejection Sampling
We briefly describe the rejection sampling algorithm, which
forms the basis of the ring toss code; see [2], [13] for
a detailed treatment. Rejection sampling simulates samples
from a target distribution P given independent and iden-
tically distributed (i.i.d.) samples {Yi}i≥1 from a proposal
distribution Q. Concretely, let r = dP/dQ and assume that
r is uniformly bounded by a constant M. Then, rejection
sampling sequentially examines the proposal samples, at each
step i accepting sample Yi with probability r(Yi)/M. Thus,
for {Ui}i≥1 i.i.d. Unif(0, 1), the uniform distribution on (0, 1),
rejection sampling returns the index

The issue is that log M can be much larger than I(X; Y ).
Essentially, this encoding is suboptimal because the uncondi-

demonstrating that, by considering the distribution of (K | Z),
we can obtain a tight upper bound on H(Y | Z). This is

sorting to adapt the encoding of rejection sampling such that
it uses at most I(X; Y ) + log(I(X; Y ) + 1) + 9 bits.
The ring toss code leverages the fact that the decoder
can compute the acceptance probability of each proposal
sample Yk under PX given its shared access to Z. This leads
to a more efficient coding distribution and hence a tighter
bound on H(Y | Z). Moreover, the probability computed is
exactly a width function, which is why the channel simulation
divergence appears in the upper bound.

VI. DISCUSSION
We have defined the ring toss code, an encoding method
for standard rejection sampling, which we prove is optimal for
relative entropy coding. In doing so, we provide a matching
achievability bound to the one-shot lower bound of Theorem
III.1 in [1]. For singular channels, our upper bound achieves
a constant redundancy over the mutual information. The ring
toss code also provides a provably tight strong functional rep-
resentation lemma [4], which has implications across a variety
of problems in lossy compression and machine learning.
There are several interesting directions of future work

Abstract: In relative entropy coding, a sender aims to design a stochastic code such that, on input X ∼PX, the receiver can generate a sample Y ∼PY |X. It is a standard result that (1) this requires at least I(X; Y ) bits, (2) the lower bound is achievable within a logarithmic gap, and (3) this gap cannot be reduced in general. The necessity of the gap suggests that the mutual information is not the correct information measure to quantify the rate of relative entropy coding. A potential alternative emerged in the work of Flamich et al. [1], who proved a tighter lower bound of IF(X →Y ), a quantity we call the functional information. In this paper, we show this lower bound is tight by constructing the ring toss code, an encoding method for rejection sampling which uses at most IF(X →Y ) + log e bits. This demonstrates that rejection sampling is optimal for relative entropy coding. Our result implies that the classical mutual information lower bound is achievable within log(I(X; Y ) + 1) + 2.45 bits in general and within 1.45 bits for singular channels, which are both the tightest bounds of their kind to date. Moreover, our one-shot result also recovers Sriramu and Wagner’s asymptotic results on the second-order redundancy of relative entropy codes.
